readme.html:
Blender Agent Studio

Describe a model, scene or animation to Codex or Claude Code. Get back an editable .blend, the Python that built it, and renders your agent has checked.

A free, open-source Blender AI plugin. It runs your local Blender and needs no extra service, API key or subscription beyond the agent you already use.

Docs · Quick start · Examples · How it works · Workflows · Development · Report a bug

A reading room built with Claude Code and Sonnet 5.5, rendered from the saved scene. It is one selected result, not an average: the paired examples show runs with and without the plugin, including failed checks and mixed visual reviews.

Quick start

You need Claude Code or Codex, Blender (5.2 LTS is the tested version) and Bun 1.3.5 or newer.

1. Install the plugin.

# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add ifBars/blender-agent-studio
claude plugin install blender-agent-studio@blender-agent-studio

# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add ifBars/blender-agent-studio
codex plugin add blender-agent-studio@blender-agent-studio

2. Check your setup. Start a new Claude Code session or Codex task and ask:

Check my Blender Agent Studio setup.

The agent runs blender_check_setup. It finds Blender, saves and reopens a tiny scene, renders a small preview image, and tells you what to fix if a step fails. It never opens your own files. Usually Blender is found automatically; if not, see point it at Blender.

3. Make something.

Use Blender Agent Studio to build a walnut desk lamp. Give it warm lighting, render it from two angles, and save the .blend and Python source.

You get an editable .blend, the Python that built it, and two renders. Open the images and judge the lamp yourself: the automated checks catch broken geometry and exports, not taste. See more to try for writing your own requests.

What you can do

  • View an open Blender session inline, orbit and zoom, and attach a clicked object to your next message with the optional Studio Live addon.
  • Build props, environments, characters, and Geometry Nodes setups.
  • Design readable signs, labels and graphic panels as editable 2D artwork, then integrate their materials and supports and review them at the intended distance. See the signage workflow.
  • Optionally record real modeling milestones and deliver a timelapse from the empty/default scene to the completed render. Ask before modeling starts; capture guide.
  • Gather references from several angles and compare the model's proportions before adding detail.
  • Overlay projected geometry on a reference image, with optional silhouette-mask measurements for missing and excess coverage. See reference modeling.
  • Rig and animate models, or work with cloth, smoke, and other simulations.
  • Render through your scene's cameras with its lighting intact, or use studio views to inspect a model from every side.
  • Download CC0 textures and HDRIs from Poly Haven at 1K, 2K, 4K, or 8K.
  • Find Mixamo motion through your browser and import downloaded FBX animations into a new .blend. See the Mixamo workflow for browser requirements and retargeting limits.
  • Find and preview Pixabay sound effects through a browser handoff. The tool provides a search URL and workflow; it does not return live results or import audio. See the MCP integration guide.
  • Check geometry and exported files, review renders, and repair what doesn't work.
  • Query scene parts and evaluated dimensions, check explicit geometry and ground constraints, and compare repairs against preserved SceneIR baselines with the optional Rust runtime.

The plugin includes twelve specialist skills and a local MCP server for inspection, rendering, and asset downloads. Generated scenes come with Python source so you can rebuild them and keep making changes. Codex and Claude Code have bundled installers today; other hosts need compatible skill loading and local execution; see portability and host requirements.

How it works

The skills guide the agent through modeling, rendering, animation, and other tasks. Blender runs locally to build or inspect the saved scene; you do not need to keep its interface open. The agent chooses the relevant steps for your request. The workflows and tools help it:

  • Turn the brief into parts, proportions, finish goals, and delivery checks. Review a graybox before spending time on materials and small details.
  • Check geometry, materials, dimensions, and other scene details. For an export, it can reopen the file in a fresh Blender process to check what survived.
  • Render a hero view plus fixed front, back, left, right, and top views. During repairs, it can use two smaller views for faster feedback before the full check.
  • Light diagnostic views with a studio setup scaled to the asset. The auto preset picks a contrasting background from simple material color hints; the agent still needs to inspect the image and adjust it when the choice fails.
  • Render through the scene's own cameras and lighting for beauty images. The tool caps resolution, samples, and render time. It offers faster preview and higher-quality final denoising policies; by default, it preserves the scene's authored denoising settings. The agent selects the policy for the job.

The .blend is the editable result. The Python source records the build steps, so you can regenerate it or ask the agent to change it later. The workflow guide explains which specialist skills apply to each kind of task. Studio views are for inspection and do not replace your scene's authored lighting in beauty renders.

Install

The quick start has the install commands. Both hosts install the same skills, MCP server, and SceneIR tools from this repository. Inside a Claude Code session, /plugin marketplace add ifBars/blender-agent-studio and /plugin install blender-agent-studio@blender-agent-studio do the same as the terminal commands.

Start a new task or session after installing or updating the plugin. Both hosts pick the relevant skill from a plain request. To name one, use $blender-agent-studio:blender-modeling-workflow in Codex or /blender-agent-studio:blender-modeling-workflow in Claude Code.

Point it at Blender

The plugin uses the first Blender it finds:

  1. A blenderPath given to a tool, or --blender on the command line.
  2. The BLENDER_EXECUTABLE environment variable.
  3. blender on your PATH.
  4. Standard install locations: the official installers on macOS (/Applications) and Windows (Program Files\Blender Foundation), Steam, and on Linux Snap, Flatpak, and archives unpacked in your home folder or /opt. When several are installed, it prefers 5.2 LTS.

A configured path that is wrong is reported, never silently replaced. For any other location, set BLENDER_EXECUTABLE to the executable itself, not its folder:

$env:BLENDER_EXECUTABLE = "C:\path\to\Blender\blender.exe"

export BLENDER_EXECUTABLE="/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender"

Launch your CLI agent from the terminal where you set the variable, or configure your desktop host's environment; a new conversation may not inherit shell changes. blender_version reports which executable was found and how.

Check from a terminal

The same setup check runs without an agent. From a repository checkout or the installed plugin directory:

bun run doctor

It saves and reopens a tiny scene, renders a 128px Cycles preview on CPU, and tries a 64px EEVEE render. It needs no API key, GPU, downloads, or Rust, and it keeps the .blend, previews, logs, and a JSON report in a new temporary folder. A failed check exits nonzero. An EEVEE warning means Cycles works but the studio inspection views need OpenGL, which headless Linux machines may lack. Use --blender "/path/to/blender" to override discovery or --output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY to keep the evidence somewhere specific. See setup troubleshooting if a check fails.

Optional and alternative installs

For the optional scene-understanding tools, build the Rust runtime in the installed plugin directory with bun run setup:runtime. See scene understanding for setup, examples and measurement limits. The other tools do not require Rust.

Update an existing GitHub installation

Codex:

codex plugin marketplace upgrade blender-agent-studio
codex plugin add blender-agent-studio@blender-agent-studio

Claude Code:

claude plugin marketplace update blender-agent-studio
claude plugin update blender-agent-studio@blender-agent-studio

Prefer skills only? See the alternative installation options and browse the workflows on skills.sh.

More to try

Include the style, dimensions, and intended use when they matter:

Build a 30 cm stylized brass lantern for a mobile game. Export a GLB and check that it imports correctly.

Here is desk.blend. Inspect it from every side, list what looks wrong, and fix the worst problem without changing anything else.

For a game asset, ask for a GLB export and an import check. For a render, you can specify a camera angle, lighting, or reference image. For a second review, ask the agent to check the result from multiple views.

How well does it work?

In five fresh, matched pairs covering a lantern, lever press, and animated drawbridge, the plugin's guided workflow passed the technical gate five times; the agent without it failed five times. Three blinded visual judges preferred the plugin asset in four of the five pairs. On one lantern repeat, all three preferred the baseline's appearance even though its geometry failed the technical gate. The plugin used more reported tokens. Lantern build time was about even across three pairs; the press and drawbridge plugin runs took about twice as long. See the current paired evidence for scores, controls, and defects.

These results show a quality gain for delivery checks on the tested prompts, with less consistent visual gains. Five pairs cannot give a reliable success rate for arbitrary prompts, models, or art styles. The three judges in each pair reviewed the same two assets; their votes are not separate generations. The comparison used the plugin's skills without its optional MCP tools, so it does not measure the extra benefit of those tools. An earlier four-task comparison also favored the plugin's final runs, but a harder integrated task had mixed results. Plugin revisions have shown both gains and regressions. Review the result yourself, particularly its shape, materials, animation, and exported files.

The five pairs above ran in Codex. The published gallery now retains 31 pairs, including later scene comparisons with Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, alongside the Codex models. The scene report records their controls, scores, visual votes, and missing reviews. Those scene results are mixed; the selected reading-room image above does not establish a general visual advantage. Each pair has one generation per condition, so the gallery is evidence to inspect rather than a general success rate.

The earlier Claude Code lantern samples had no baseline and remain separate from those paired scene comparisons. Keep each result tied to its tested host, model, task, and plugin revision.

Support development

If Blender Agent Studio helps you build or inspect scenes, consider supporting its maintainer through GitHub Sponsors or Ko-fi. Contributions help sustain the time spent on Blender and agent compatibility, reproducible examples, bug fixes, and benchmark runs that report failures as well as improvements.

The plugin stays free, MIT-licensed, and runs Blender locally. Sponsorship is optional and does not purchase priority support or feature commitments. Sharing a scene, reporting a reproducible bug, or improving the docs also helps.

Star history

Contributing

Found a bug? Open an issue with your Blender version, what you asked for, and what happened. A render or error log helps.

Made something with the plugin? Share an example with your prompt, agent/model, Blender version, and a render. If you want it featured in the docs, say so and include the build script when you can. Only share files you have permission to publish.

For code changes, see the development guide and repository instructions. Keep generated models and benchmark output out of commits. Review unfamiliar Blender scripts before running them; see security notes.

Credits and license

This is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Blender Foundation or Poly Haven. See third-party notices.
